title: Register Sizes & Purposes
description:
## Register Sizes
Every register comes in multiple sizes:
```
rax  = 64-bit (full register)
eax  = 32-bit (lower half of rax)
ax   = 16-bit (lower half of eax)
ah   = 8-bit  (upper byte of ax)
al   = 8-bit  (lower byte of ax)
```
Same pattern for all: `rbx/ebx/bx/bh/bl`, `rcx/ecx/cx/ch/cl`, etc.

For `r8`-`r15` the suffixes are different: `r8/r8d/r8w/r8b`.

Use the smallest size that fits your data. Reading a byte from memory? `al`. Doing a syscall? `rax`. Working with addresses? `rax` (addresses are 64-bit).

## Register Purposes
- `rax` - syscall number, return values, general math
- `rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9` - function/syscall arguments (in that order)
- `rsp` - stack pointer (don't touch unless you know what you're doing)
- `rbp` - base pointer (stack frame)
- `rbx, r12-r15` - preserved across function calls
- `r10, r11` - scratch registers
